title: APR Targets 3,200 Walmart Stores As Medicube Retail Push Accelerates
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

APR Corp. is pushing Medicube deeper into the US retail mainstream, marking a major offline expansion for the South Korean cosmetics and home-beauty device maker as it tries to turn viral demand into broader consumer access. The company is preparing to roll out Medicube products to about 3,200 Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) stores in June, while also holding talks to bring the range to Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ:COST) warehouses across the US, Canada and Europe in the second half of the year. APR's products already debuted in more than 1,500 Target (NYSE:TGT) stores in April, giving the company another large retail channel as it moves beyond the online-first strategy that had leaned heavily on Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), TikTok Shop and Ulta Beauty (NASDAQ:ULTA) as its only significant brick-and-mortar partner.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with BA. Is WMT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The shift could materially widen APR's physical reach, with the company expecting global points of sale to rise to between 5,000 and 6,000, more than three times its current footprint. That matters because APR is moving at a time when more Korean beauty companies are chasing overseas shelf space, with CJ Olive Young set to open its first US store in California this month after securing a partnership with LVMH-owned Sephora. Walmart and Costco declined to comment, but APR's planned retail buildout suggests the company is trying to convert Medicube's digital strength into a broader physical presence across some of the most important consumer markets.

Investor attention is already high. Strong global demand for APR's flagship Medicube line has helped lift the company's market value to nearly 16 trillion won, or about $11 billion, surpassing Amorepacific and Shiseido and making APR one of Asia's most valuable cosmetics makers. The company is scheduled to report first-quarter earnings on Thursday and has set a 2026 revenue target of 2.1 trillion won, a 40% increase from the previous year, with an expected operating margin of about 25%. Shares have climbed about 80% so far this year, while overseas markets accounted for about 80% of total revenue last year. APR is also aiming to replicate its online success in Europe after entering the UK last year, with plans to expand through Amazon into France, Germany, Italy and Spain through 2026. The opportunity could be meaningful, but the risks remain real: the US beauty market is highly competitive, consumers are facing cost-of-living pressure, and some investors have raised concerns that selling through both retail partners and direct-to-consumer channels could possibly dilute the brand's positioning. Still, Korea Investment & Securities analyst Kim Myoungjoo said those concerns may be overstated given the relatively low overseas penetration of Korean beauty brands, particularly in Europe, and said the retail expansion will serve as a fresh US sales catalyst while broader European access is expected to help cement APR's status as a global beauty powerhouse.

title: Amazon Adds Same-Day Ozempic Pill Delivery
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Amazon (AMZN, Financials) announced Novo Nordisk's new Ozempic pill will be accessible on Amazon Pharmacy and can be delivered the same day, as the retailer continues to expand into health care and access to prescription drugs.The once-daily oral diabetic therapy also will be delivered through in-office kiosks at certain One Medical primary care clinics, enabling qualified patients to obtain the medicine soon after visits.Amazon announced it will offer same-day delivery in over 3,000 U.S. cities and towns, whether customers are Prime members or not. The company intends to grow the service to about 4,500 places by the end of 2026.Novo Nordisk re-branded their oral GLP-1 medication Rybelsus to launch the Ozempic tablet earlier this week. individuals with insurance will pay as little as $25 per month for the first dose, while cash-paying individuals can get the starting dose for $149 per month.For investors, the deal bolsters Amazon's pharmacy play and gives Novo Nordisk another distribution channel in the fast-growing GLP-1 space.

title: Microsoft Reconsiders Energy Goal Amid AI Boom
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) is reportedly reconsidering one of its biggest climate goals as the AI driven data center boom pushes energy demand to new levels.

According to reports, the company is discussing whether to delay or potentially abandon its 2030 target of matching 100% of its hourly electricity usage with renewable energy purchases. The conversations are still ongoing and no final decision has been made, but the debate itself highlights how quickly AI infrastructure demands are reshaping energy priorities across Big Tech.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 1 Warning Sign with MSFT. Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The challenge comes down to scale. Microsoft has been adding nearly 1 gigawatt of data center capacity every 3 months as it races to support AI and cloud growth. That rapid expansion is increasing both electricity usage and emissions, despite major renewable energy investments. Since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022, Microsoft's emissions have reportedly risen 23%, with the company itself pointing to AI and cloud expansion as major contributors.

At the same time, the industry is increasingly leaning toward natural gas to meet near term power needs. Companies like Amazon (AMZN), Meta (META) and Google (GOOG) are also facing growing pressure as AI workloads surge. Microsoft says it remains committed to its long term sustainability ambitions, but also acknowledged that adjustments may be needed as markets and technology evolve.
